guard: Five quiet seconds before each run; reject overlap with a foreign process consuming more than one CPU core in a sampled interval after allowing two scheduler ticks of accounting precision. Per-process timestamps avoid proc-scan timing skew. Small background-service bursts remain ordinary host noise.
workload: Unchanged YCSB-A: 100M load, complete 400M transactions, 31 foreground + 1 background
policy: evidence-balanced-size-tiebreaker.config; automatic seed selection; no companion/adaptive/partial placement
memory: GNU time %M: whole-process peak RSS in KiB. Runtime residency: selected private heap pages, not whole-process RSS. No smaps walk or debugger in throughput runs.
checks: Native IR, rewritten IR, complete seed report, native executable and Arbiter executable are byte-identical before/after cleanup. 14 retained fixture commands match baseline; existing compiler/runtime smoke passed; removed option rejected.
guard_correction: Initial whole-scan timestamps and zero tick tolerance rejected one-core accounting jitter. Final suite uses per-process sample times plus two ticks of accounting tolerance; all earlier processes excluded.
source_edits: Removed one micro-specific published-RMW scoring parameter and analysis; no benchmark or runtime source edits.
swap_evidence: All processes run with MemorySwapMax=0; all six smaps snapshots show Swap=0. GNU time %W is recorded but is not independent swap evidence on Linux.
limitations: Three full runs per mode on one monitored shared host. Whole-process peak RSS includes setup/validation, not only timed replay. Diagnostic snapshots are separate processes, not peak-RSS measurements. No historical throughput pooling.
